newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU report to show cereals farmers over-paid.
newsitem.headline: EU report to show cereals farmers over-paid.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to present a report this week showing that cereals farmers have been paid some eight billion Ecus too much over the past four years for price cuts that never happened.

EU diplomats said the Commission told a weekly meeting of member state agriculture officials that it agreed with a British memorandum in April that farmers had been over-paid, although its figure was much less than Britain's 17 billion Ecus.
"It's a signal that the Commission will insist on cutting cereals aid," said one diplomat.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has proposed a 1.4 billion Ecus cut in aid to cereals farmers to help beef farmers hit by the mad cow crisis.
The proposal, which is opposed by nearly all member states, will be discussed by farm ministers in Luxembourg from June 22-25 along with the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package.
They argue that the cuts are not needed because of an estimated one billion Ecus underspend in the 1997 budget.
